system_description.narrative_title: Regional escalation around Gaza amid US mediation
system_description.narrative_summary: An open system of escalating cross-border violence and diplomatic intervention: Israeli strikes in Gaza, Syria and Lebanon interact with US-led mediation efforts (Kushner, Trump envoys), regional deconfliction talks and international criticism. Feedback loops link battlefield actions, domestic Israeli politics, humanitarian crises and diplomatic initiatives — military moves provoke diplomatic responses and vice versa, while external actors (US, Turkey, UN, Syria, Lebanon) transmit resources, pressure and constraints into the system. The system is porous to inputs (arms, funding, political pressure, public opinion) and outputs (refugee flows, international condemnation, security incidents) that reshape its evolution.
system_description.scope: The Israel–Gaza conflict and its immediate regional spillovers: Israeli military operations in Gaza, cross-border strikes into Syria and Lebanon, West Bank settler violence, Israeli domestic political dynamics affecting strategy, US mediation and deconfliction efforts (Kushner, Trump envoys, US envoy), UN/peacekeeping and international humanitarian responses, and investigations into military conduct.
system_description.super_system: Middle East regional security and international diplomatic order (US-led diplomacy, UN mechanisms, regional powers and alliances)
adjacent_subsystems: Israeli domestic politics and coalition dynamics
Palestinian governance and humanitarian systems (Gaza, West Bank)
Syrian and Lebanese security complex (Assad regime, Hezbollah, Turkish operations)

variables.name: Cross-border strikes
variables.description: Measures the intensity and frequency of armed strikes and engagements that cross recognized boundaries within the regional system.

variables.name: Internal violence
variables.description: Measures the level of armed violence within territories, including raids, ground operations, and local clashes.

variables.name: Diplomatic mediation
variables.description: Measures the intensity and persistence of third-party negotiation, mediation and shuttle diplomacy efforts within the system.

variables.name: Deconfliction mechanisms
variables.description: Measures the presence and effectiveness of communication channels and tacit or formal agreements designed to prevent unintended military clashes.

variables.name: Arms and munition flows
variables.description: Measures the volume and rate of weapons, munitions and military materiel transfers into the operational area.

variables.name: External funding level
variables.description: Measures the magnitude and volatility of external financial and material support available to conflict actors.

variables.name: Humanitarian crisis severity
variables.description: Measures cumulative indicators of humanitarian need, including shortages of food, water, shelter and medical care.

variables.name: Displaced population
variables.description: Measures the number of internally displaced persons and refugees generated by the conflict.

variables.name: Casualty rate
variables.description: Measures the rate of fatalities and serious injuries occurring per unit time that are attributable to hostilities.

variables.name: Public support for hostilities
variables.description: Measures the level of domestic public approval for continued or escalated military action among affected populations.

variables.name: International condemnation pressure
variables.description: Measures the intensity of diplomatic criticism, sanctions pressure and reputational costs imposed by external actors and global publics.

variables.name: Security incident frequency
variables.description: Measures the frequency of discrete security incidents such as attacks, infiltrations and violent confrontations per time period.

variables.name: Peacekeeping and monitoring presence
variables.description: Measures the scale and operational capacity of neutral monitoring, peacekeeping and de‑escalation deployments in the area.

variables.name: Legal and accountability processes
variables.description: Measures the activity and effectiveness of investigations, prosecutions and oversight mechanisms addressing alleged misconduct and rights abuses.

variables.name: Humanitarian access levels
variables.description: Measures the degree to which humanitarian actors can reach affected populations with aid, services and protection.

variables.name: Perceived ceasefire stability
variables.description: Measures the perceived durability and credibility of temporary pauses or ceasefire understandings among stakeholders and mediators.
